content.title: Gretna City Council approves new I-80 interchange road improvements
content.text: A total of 23 states reduced their top marginal rate, or the highest tax rate a person pays on their taxable income, taking effect in 2026. Seven states have shifted from graduated-rate systems to flat-rate systems, where all taxable income is subject to the same tax rate regardless of income.This is according to a study by the independent tax policy research organization Tax Foundation, that ranked states by how their taxes are structured. Income tax is a government levy on individuals and businesses based on taxable income. There are two types: the uniform federal tax and the state income tax, which funds public services such as education, transportation and health care. State taxes vary widely, some states have no income tax, others have flat rates and some use graduated-rate systems where higher-income earners pay more taxes. States that have reduced their top rateAlaskaArizonaColoradoFloridaGeorgiaIdahoIllinoisIndianaIowaKentuckyLouisianaMichiganMississippiNevadaNew HampshireNorth CarolinaOhioPennsylvaniaSouth DakotaUtahTennesseeTexasWyoming Nicole Fox, a policy analyst for the Tax Foundation, said states have been making these reforms for decades, but the trend we are seeing now started because of COVID-19. During the pandemic, states had a surplus in tax revenue that allowed them to pursue income tax relief. Factors included federal aid, stimulus checks to individuals, inflation, which increased sales tax revenue, and higher wages that led to increased income tax revenue.When some states started to reduce their income tax rates, others followed suit. "I think the main thing that’s driving the trend toward income tax rate reductions really is just pure old-fashioned competition. States are competing for people, they’re competing for businesses, whether it’s established businesses hoping that they will expand within the state or it’s trying to attract new businesses, new entrepreneurs and startups," Fox said. States with low to no income tax The average top individual rate has started to decline, averaging 5% in 2026, according to the Tax Foundation. Arizona and North Dakota have the lowest income tax rate at 2.5%. This is followed by Ohio at 2.75% and Indiana at 2.95%. Nine states currently do not have an income tax: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington and Wyoming.But for states that do not have income tax, Fox said this does not mean they do not have higher local collections."For example, Florida and Texas, both no income state taxes, but they are states that have a very heavy reliance on property taxes. And if you look at Florida, there's a high reliance on tourism, and so you have a lot of a big influx of nonresidents spending more money in-state," said Fox. Which states have raised taxes?Fox also noted a divergence in the trend. As more states have lowered their top rates, others have moved to increase their top rate. This includes states such as Maryland, Massachusetts and New York, and the District of Columbia. California has proposed a ballot initiative for a wealth tax called the "2026 California Billionaire Tax Act," which would impose a one-time wealth tax of 5% on billionaires living in California. Revenues from the wealth tax would be set aside for health care. California has the highest top marginal state personal income tax rate, at 13.3%.Washington state, which currently does not have a wage and income tax, recently passed a high-earner tax in March. The "millionaires’ tax" imposes a 9.9% tax on personal income over $1 million and will take effect in 2028."Taxes for a lot of people, the cost of living, does drive decisions on where to work, where to live, where to start a business. And most definitely, the trend is people are leaving high tax environments for lower tax environments," said Fox.
